sanity_expectations: v is monotone increasing in S over the sampled range
v -> 0 as S -> 0 (limit ~ (Vmax/Km)*S in the low-S regime)
v approaches the finite asymptote Vmax as S -> infinity (saturates near S >> Km)
v(S=Km) = Vmax/2 (half-maximal velocity at S = Km)
v is bounded in [0, Vmax] and stays real and finite over S in [0.01, 100]
excitation_report: Single term S*Vmax/(Km+S) reaches RMS 0.627, i.e. 31.4x sigma over S in [0.01, 100] (log-sampled) with Vmax=1, Km=1. Well above the 5x threshold across the region. No parent term to compare against (gen 0).
role_corrections: v: O->O (confirmed as dependent variable, LHS of explicit relation)
S: V->V (confirmed as independent axis; substrate concentration is the swept assay variable)
Vmax: V->P (overridden: physical constant of the enzyme preparation, fixed per assay, not an axis)
Km: V->P (overridden: intrinsic enzyme affinity constant, fixed per assay, not an axis)
rationale: Classic Michaelis-Menten kinetics: v is explicitly solved from the RHS S*Vmax/(Km+S), so equation_type=explicit and integrator=evaluate_explicit. Only S is swept experimentally (varied substrate concentration at fixed enzyme); Vmax and Km are intrinsic to the enzyme/preparation and are held constant across the titration, so they are parameters, not axes. Using Vmax=Km=1 puts the curve's inflection near S=Km=1; sampling S log-uniformly from 0.01 to 100 (i.e. 0.01*Km to 100*Km) resolves both the linear regime v ~ (Vmax/Km)*S at low S and the saturation plateau v -> Vmax at high S, matching the phenomenon description. Absolute noise sigma=0.02 is ~2% of Vmax — small enough to leave the saturation plateau and the low-S linear regime clearly distinguishable, while forcing the fit to actually capture the hyperbolic curvature rather than a straight line.
